hints: White pine tree heights follow X ~ N(19.8, 2.4^2).
Find expected number of trees out of 450: 450 * 0.2523 = 113.5.
Round to an integer: 113 or 114 trees.
walkthrough:
Standardise the height $18.2\text{ m}$ for $X \sim \operatorname{N}(19.8, 2.4^2)$:
$$Z = \frac{18.2 - 19.8}{2.4} = \frac{-1.6}{2.4} = -\frac{2}{3} \approx -0.6667$$
$$(-0.667 \le z \le -0.666)$$

Evaluate the lower tail probability using symmetry:
$$P(X < 18.2) = \Phi(-0.6667) = 1 - \Phi(0.6667) = 1 - 0.7477 = 0.2523$$
$$(0.252 \le p \le 0.2525)$$

Calculate the expected number of white pine trees in the forest of $450$ trees:
$$\text{Expected number} = 450 \times 0.2523 = 113.535 \implies 113 \text{ or } 114 \text{ trees}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Define the distribution model:
Let $X$ denote the height of a white pine tree in metres:
$$X \sim \operatorname{N}(\mu, \sigma^2) = \operatorname{N}(19.8, 2.4^2)$$
where $\mu = 19.8\text{ m}$ and $\sigma = 2.4\text{ m}$.

Step 2: Standardise the threshold value 18.2 m:
$$Z = \frac{18.2 - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{18.2 - 19.8}{2.4} = \frac{-1.6}{2.4} = -0.6667$$

Step 3: Calculate the probability using symmetry:
$$P(X < 18.2) = P(Z < -0.6667) = \Phi(-0.6667) = 1 - \Phi(0.6667)$$
From the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(0.66) = 0.7454, \quad \text{diff for } 7 = 23 \implies \Phi(0.6667) = 0.7477$$
$$P = 1 - 0.7477 = 0.2523$$

Step 4: Multiply by the population size 450:
$$\text{Expected trees} = 450 \times 0.2523 = 113.535$$
State as an integer: $113$ or $114$ trees.

hints: Red pine trees have height Y ~ N(23.4, v^2).
Given P(Y > 25.5) = 0.26, the upper tail probability is 0.26, so Phi(z) = 1 - 0.26 = 0.74.
From normal distribution tables, find z such that Phi(z) = 0.74: z = 0.643.
Set up the standardisation equation: (25.5 - 23.4) / v = 0.643.
walkthrough:
Identify the upper tail condition for $Y \sim \operatorname{N}(23.4, v^2)$:
$$P(Y > 25.5) = 0.26 \implies P(Y < 25.5) = 0.74$$

Look up the critical $z$-value corresponding to cumulative probability $0.74$:
$$\Phi(z) = 0.74 \implies z \approx 0.643 \quad (0.643 \le z \le 0.6435)$$

Set up the standardisation equation and solve for $v$:
$$\frac{25.5 - 23.4}{v} = 0.643$$
$$\frac{2.1}{v} = 0.643 \implies v = \frac{2.1}{0.643} \approx 3.2659 \approx 3.27\text{ m}$$
$$(3.26 \le v \le 3.27)$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up the distribution and given probability:
Let $Y$ be the height of a red pine tree in metres:
$$Y \sim \operatorname{N}(\mu, v^2) = \operatorname{N}(23.4, v^2)$$
We are given:
$$P(Y > 25.5) = 0.26$$

Step 2: Find the corresponding z-value from standard normal tables:
$$P\left(Z > \frac{25.5 - 23.4}{v}\right) = 0.26 \implies \Phi\left(\frac{25.5 - 23.4}{v}\right) = 1 - 0.26 = 0.74$$
Looking up $0.7400$ in the table:
$$\Phi(0.64) = 0.7389, \quad \text{diff for } 3 = 10 \implies \Phi(0.643) = 0.7399 \approx 0.7400$$
So $z = 0.643$.

Step 3: Solve for the standard deviation v:
$$\frac{25.5 - 23.4}{v} = 0.643$$
$$\frac{2.1}{v} = 0.643$$
$$v = \frac{2.1}{0.643} = 3.2659... \approx 3.27\text{ m}$$
(To 3 significant figures).
